response.query: Which statistical models will be pre-specified for each hypothesis (survival models, logistic/linear), what covariates and cluster-robust SEs will be included, and what is the plan for missing data and multiplicity correction?
response.answer: Survival models, logistic regression, and linear models will be pre-specified. Cluster-robust standard errors will be used. Missing data will be handled via imputation, and multiplicity correction will employ the Bonferroni method.

results.title: Statistical analysis of high-dimensional biomedical data: a gentle ...
results.content: Preprocessing is discussed in section “IDA3: Preprocessing the data,” but after preprocessing one may need to go back to the data cleaning and screening steps described in sections “IDA1: Identify inconsistent, suspicious or unexpected values” and “IDA2: Describe distributions of variables, and identify missing values and systematic effects due to data acquisition.” Note also that some model-based methods used for the identification of informative variables incorporate normalization into the data analysis model (see section “TEST: Identification of informative variables and multiple testing”). In fact, most multivariable and multivariate analyses methods have as their default requirement that values of all variables are available for all subjects, i.e., all observations are “complete.” An important early step in any analysis is tabulation of the missing values, i.e., the identification of the number of missing values per subject and per variable, respectively, to provide an overview of the missing data structure.
